assessment: This deck carries no sideboard, so all ten are pool scouts — the deck's first pool read, drawn from 11,831 eligible cards and ranked to extend the two engines stack 001 already verified: the Yawgmoth undying loop and the Snake-minting counter converter. The top half stacks bodies and payoffs that ride those loops — 'redundancy is cheap per slot and live every game' [strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors] — the back half fills the role budget's draw and sweeper shortfalls. Three famous names stay off on a read of the card: The Great Henge (rank 235) prices off greatest power and a board of 1/1 Snakes leaves it near nine mana; Gravecrawler's graveyard clause needs a Zombie and the deck controls exactly one (Host of the Hereafter); Triskelion adds little because stack 001 step 15 shows in-deck Walking Ballista already runs the same Mikaeus line as a three-card assembly with any of the deck's eight free outlets.

ten.why: Nest of Scarabs mints black Insects, so every batch of -1/-1 counters becomes a table-wide Ayara drain, and her tagged line rides the Yawgmoth-plus-Mikaeus engine stack 001 verified as a library-bounded loop.
ten.unlocks: A drain trigger on every Insect and undying return, plus sac-a-black-body card draw between combats.

ten.why: Pay 1 life, sacrifice another creature, get a Treasure: every Snake the commander mints becomes a mana, no combo required — and the tagged Mikaeus line must clear stack 001's finding that counter-neutral outlets stall undying after one return.
ten.unlocks: Converts the token engine into ramp, and puts a second Zombie on the battlefield.

ten.why: Stack 001 proved a sacrificed token never comes back; this card creature returns for {1}{B}, and with in-deck Pitiless Plunderer plus either altar the channel tags the recursion as mana-neutral fodder — both partners already sleeved.
ten.unlocks: Repeatable sacrifice fodder for Yawgmoth, Viscera Seer, and Carrion Feeder that survives the token rule.

ten.why: A non-Human Zombie body for the verified Yawgmoth loop — each undying return is a fresh devotion drain — and a fair turn-5 cast still hits the table off a black-heavy board.
ten.unlocks: The finisher the Yawgmoth engine currently lacks: its library-bounded loop ends games before the library does.

ten.why: The role budget is two sweepers short, and this one is on-theme: a -1/-1 counter on each creature one opponent controls feeds Hapatra and Nest of Scarabs, hands Necroskitter everything that dies, and the double proliferate grows every counter already on the table.
ten.unlocks: A one-sided sweep that pays the deck's own engines instead of fighting them.

ten.why: The budget says draw is two short; Braids feeds a spare Snake or Insect each end step and every opponent either sacrifices along or pays 2 life and a card — an engine running on fodder the commander mints for free.
ten.unlocks: Turns surplus tokens into cards without spending mana or a combat.

ten.why: Three mana whose ETB alone makes a Snake off Hapatra and two Insects off Nest of Scarabs; aim the two counters at a spare 1/1 and Blowfly Infestation passes a counter on when it dies — the tagged Mikaeus line still owes a stack scenario.
ten.unlocks: A menace body that pays the deck's counter engines on entry and drains on Zombie deaths.

ten.why: The channel's most popular opener (40,311 saves) with in-deck Orcish Bowmasters: half a library of forced draws under Bowmasters' trigger — not called a kill until a stack scenario says so, and Dark Ritual plus two altars make seven mana honest here.
ten.unlocks: A one-slot line to delete the problem opponent using a partner already sleeved.

ten.why: Name Snake and every token the commander mints replaces itself on death through the eight free sacrifice outlets stack 001's census counted — the second half of the draw shortfall.
ten.unlocks: Card draw priced in bodies the deck already produces as a by-product.

ten.why: The obsolescence index's cleanest hit on this list: zero mana against Grim Monolith's two, and a two-mana commander plus eight other legendaries means it taps for colour from turn 2 most games — while cutting the Monolith retires a Game Changer without moving the computed floor.
ten.unlocks: Free acceleration into the deck's turn-2-to-4 engine window.

gaps: The Mikaeus lines tagged for Warren Soultrader and Plague Belcher pair him with counter-neutral outlets, which stack 001 showed stall undying after one return; a stack scenario per line would settle whether anything loops.

Contagion Engine's Snake yield reads as one Snake per creature hit (each creature is a separate counter-placement for Hapatra's trigger); a stack scenario would pin the exact count on a mass placement.
The role budget driving the draw and sweeper picks is provisional and uncited by its own note — treated as a lead, not evidence.
Gravecrawler (six tagged lines, the channel's widest opener) sat out for want of Zombies; if Warren Soultrader and Gray Merchant come in, the count reaches three and the pick deserves a re-rank.
